findings.defect: The exhibited reduction does NOT decide SSG-Compare, and its two selling points ("a single oracle call and six vertices", "the simpler of the two") are bought exactly by omitting the tie-breaking that thm:top pays O(a) vertices for. SSG-Compare, as used at thm:compare-equivalence and prop:no-halving(b) and in the non-adaptive half of thm:compare-equivalence, is the NON-STRICT question val(p) >= val(q). The route's own proof concedes that at val_G(p) = val_G(q) the argmax set is {m_p, m_q}; a correct TopC oracle may then return m_q, from which the reduction cannot distinguish "<" from "=" and must answer NO where the truth is YES. "Up to the harmless tie" is not harmless: it is precisely the case the target needs. Repairing it needs a strict offset below the minimum gap between distinct values, which is 4^{-a} by lem:denominator-sharp, i.e. a chain of Theta(a) fresh average vertices -- exactly thm:top's reference and boost chains. Repaired, fs16:topctrl is thm:top with 'average' replaced by 'controlled' at the same asymptotic cost, and the concluding remark's contrast with thm:top is backwards.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.9086 (thm:compare-equivalence) and l.9280 (prop:no-halving(b)) both state SSG-Compare as "w*(x) >= w*(y)"; thm:top's proof at l.9398-9425 spends r = 2a+2 reference-chain vertices and 2m boost vertices precisely so that "the maximiser is unique and names c_p^{(m)} exactly when val(p) >= val(q)". The route's own proof text: "{m_p,m_q} if =. A single oracle call therefore decides val_G(p) >= val_G(q) up to the harmless tie."

The sentence after prop:modulator-family asks for an AMORTISATION -- 'the O(B^{k+1}) payoff vectors at which a separator node queries its children during one search can be answered in total time polynomially related to the time to answer one of them' -- and the paper explicitly adds 'the other route to it, a bound on the number of pieces of the response, is closed by rem:fold-width'. fs16 proves a statement about the NUMBER OF PIECES (two, at interface dimension zero), i.e. about the route the paper had already closed, and proves nothing about amortising queries. At interface dimension zero there is nothing to amortise -- one query answers everything -- so the positive half is empty; at dimension one the amortisation question is exactly where thm:qp left it. findings.defect: Invalid inference. 'H<C_theta> has at least s vertices. So a black-box composition multiplies the quantity to be resolved by at most O(s) while multiplying the size by at least s' -- the composed game has s + (#calls)(|G|-1) vertices, so when the context has O(1) calls the size is INCREASED BY s, not multiplied by s, while the gap bound still permits a factor (4/3)(s+3). The conclusion 'the ratio gap/size is not improved by more than a constant factor, whatever the context' therefore follows only for contexts with Theta(s) calls (automata), not 'whatever the context'; whether a bounded-call context can realise derivative Theta(s) is not addressed. thm:fs16-noamp itself is unaffected -- it is the statement that carries the weight -- but this corollary should be deleted or re-scoped.

verdict:
SPLIT. The main line is real mathematics, but it is not the headline the route thinks it is, and two subsidiary results are wrong as stated.

WHAT IS SOUND AND NEW. I re-derived the two hardest items independently and both hold in exact arithmetic: the qualitative fixed points (4000 random SSGs, 2910 non-stopping, agreeing with brute-force wstar) and the energy identity sum_v N_v Delta_v^2 = 4w(1-w) with sum_v N_v |Delta_v| <= r+2 (784 random stopping games, worst ratio 4/15); the gate lemma too (387 honest compositions, 114 with p != q). fs16:cross is genuinely new here and its Doob step is load-bearing: the naive coupling bound sum_v N_v |dp| is exponential -- rem:impedance's own chain has expected visits 2^{Theta(N)} -- so the crossing argument is what turns an exponential Lipschitz constant into a linear one. cor:fs16-visits (N_v <= Delta_v^{-2} at an average vertex under an optimal pair) is a clean invariant the paper lacks. And q := val_{G^rev}(v0) = min_sigma max_tau Pr[t1] is the one genuinely new OBJECT the route produces: it is not lem:duality's 1 - val, and the paper never uses it.

WHAT IS NOT. The headline -- fs16:noamp and fs16:noqual -- covers none of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6, def:bsi, R_BR or all-switches, and, worse, the black-box class it constrains contains no reduction that appears anywhere in frontier.tex: thm:stopping-transform, thm:compare-equivalence's G-united-with-G-bar, lem:normalform, def:freeze, lem:splice and thm:top's own construction all read the input's edges and are outside def:fs16-context. It is not merely a barrier against an unpursued programme; it is a barrier against a class from which every construction this document performs is excluded. fs16:two misdescribes the paper's amortisation open item (the paper had already closed the pieces route at rem:fold-width and asks a different question, which fs16 does not touch). fs16:topctrl's reduction does not decide SSG-Compare's non-strict >= on a tie, and its \"six vertices, one call\" advantage over thm:top is exactly the Theta(a) tie-breaking thm:top pays for. cor:fs16-gapratio's inference (\"multiplying the size by at least s\") is invalid.

THE TRUE REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it. Not \"does every reduction to almost-sure reachability factor through a context composition\". The true gap is one level up: the route proved a sensitivity bound for the one-parameter family {H^{p,q}} in which the input game is never inspected, and has exhibited no candidate algorithm, reduction or mechanism -- in this document or outside it -- that lies in that family; so the two impossibility statements have no known nonempty extension, and the statement that would give them one (that some interesting reduction is a black-box composition) is neither proved nor plausible.

BETTER OR WORSE? As submitted, WORSE: about six pages added to a 176-page, 412-result document, whose headline is a barrier over an empty extension, and which contains one false theorem (fs16:topctrl) and one misstatement of the paper's own open item (fs16:two).

TRIMMED, BETTER -- and the trim is easy. INTEGRATE: (1) lem:fs16-positive and thm:fs16-assure with the \"naive version is false\" warning, into sec:simorder, justified by thm:top rather than by def:simorder -- thm:top genuinely needs the EXACT {val=1}, whereas def:simorder tolerates under-approximations; while integrating, also repair def:simorder's one-line description of Z_0, which I verified is itself only an under-approximation on the 2-vertex stopping game u in Vmin -> (t1,x), x in Vavg -> (u,t0) (the Min clause is missing, exactly as in the naive Z_1 algorithm the route refutes). (2) lem:fs16-gate in the (p,q) form, with q named and flagged as the new quantity, plus the route's own open question (is q easier than p? are p and q jointly constrained?). (3) thm:fs16-contract next to rem:fold-width, WITHOUT rem:fs16-two's amortisation sentence and WITHOUT the polynomial class. (4) thm:fs16-cross, cor:fs16-visits, cor:fs16-lip and rem:fs16-blind as a short subsection, with one sentence attributing (a) to the classical quadratic-variation identity. DEMOTE to a single half-page remark, labelled as covering none of the mechanisms of sec:gap in the style the paper already uses at cor:gate: cor:fs16-bias, thm:fs16-noamp, thm:fs16-noqual, rem:fs16-iid, rem:fs16-measured, rem:fs16-scope. DO NOT INTEGRATE: thm:fs16-topctrl (false as stated; repaired it duplicates thm:top at the same cost), cor:fs16-gapratio (invalid), rem:fs16-two's class, and lem:fs16-mixmin / prop:fs16-mixmono (one DEAD-list line instead).

Verification honesty: no defect found; sampling is used only to check separately proved statements, the harness respects both standing traps, and the route volunteers its own refuted first attempt and its blindness on WD and CC.
